edges.description: TGF-beta, IL-4, IL-13, and connective tissue growth factor drive activated fibroblasts to deposit excess extracellular matrix and collagen in the fascia.
Progressive collagen deposition and thickening of the deep fascia and subcutaneous septa cause woody skin induration and joint flexion contractures.
Fibrotic thickening of the deep fascia and subcutaneous septa produces symmetric woody skin induration of the extremities.
Tethering of the dermis by fibrotic subcutaneous septa produces a dimpled peau d'orange appearance.
Unchecked fascial fibrosis across joint planes restricts range of motion and produces flexion contractures.
Fibrotic tethering of the deep fascia spares the superficial dermis, producing linear venous furrowing (groove sign) upon limb elevation.

nodes.description: A triggering insult (commonly strenuous exertion, drug exposure such as immune checkpoint inhibitors, or infection) drives a Th2-skewed immune response in the deep fascia with recruitment of eosinophils and T cells. Eosinophils are detected within the fascia and degranulate, releasing effector molecules. Activators of the Th2-M2 pathway (STAT6, IL-4) are upregulated at the muscle-fascia interface.
